title: Network & Wi-Fi
blurb: No internet, slow or dropping Wi-Fi, can't see other computers.

remedies.title: Hotel or café Wi-Fi sign-in page doesn't appear
symptoms: guest wifi terms page not showing
remedies.why: Public Wi-Fi shows a sign-in page before letting you online; a VPN, a custom DNS or an open secure site can stop it appearing.

steps.text: Open a plain web address like http://neverssl.com in the browser; it redirects to the sign-in page.
Turn off the VPN and any custom DNS (like 1.1.1.1 apps) until you've signed in.
Forget the network and join again to trigger the sign-in prompt.
If the page still won't appear, try another browser or a private window.

remedies.title: Change the DNS server (for example to 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8)
remedies.why: DNS turns names into addresses. Your provider's DNS is used by default; a public one can be faster or fix name lookup failures.

steps.text: Settings › Network & internet › Wi-Fi (or Ethernet) › Hardware properties › DNS server assignment › Edit › Manual, add 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8.
Network › your connection › Details › DNS › + to add 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8.
Clear the old answers afterwards.
On work computers leave DNS alone: company sites often only resolve through the company's DNS.

remedies.escalate: Work devices: ask IT before changing DNS.

remedies.title: Find my computer's IP address or MAC address
remedies.why: IT or a router setting often needs this computer's network address (IP) or hardware address (MAC).

steps.text: Settings › Network & internet › Wi-Fi (or Ethernet) › Hardware properties: IPv4 address and Physical address (MAC).
Network › your connection › Details: IP address under TCP/IP, MAC under Hardware.
Your public (internet) IP is different; search "what is my IP" to see it.
Wi-Fi may show a private (random) MAC per network; turn it off for that network if IT needs the real one.

remedies.title: See the password of the Wi-Fi I'm connected to
remedies.why: The computer remembers the password of networks you joined; you can look it up to share it.

steps.text: Settings › Network & internet › Wi-Fi › your network's properties › View Wi-Fi security key.
Wi-Fi settings › ⋯ next to the network › Copy Password, or Keychain Access › search the network › Show password.
Phones can share it: iPhone near a Mac with the same Apple Account offers Share Password; Android shows a QR code.

remedies.title: Updates or OneDrive won't download (metered connection)
remedies.why: On a connection marked as metered, Windows and OneDrive hold back big downloads to save data.

steps.text: Turn off Metered connection for this network unless you're on a phone hotspot or limited plan.
Check data limits: Settings › Network & internet › Data usage.

remedies.title: Computer keeps joining the wrong Wi-Fi
remedies.why: It auto-joins every network it remembers; a weak or guest network can win.

steps.text: Turn off "Connect automatically" for the network you don't want, or forget it.
Wi-Fi settings › ⓘ next to the network › turn off Auto-Join, or Forget it.

remedies.title: Wi-Fi is weak in some rooms
remedies.why: Walls, floors and distance weaken Wi-Fi, especially 5 GHz.

steps.text: Place the router high and central, out of cupboards and away from TVs and metal.
Use 2.4 GHz for range, 5 GHz for speed near the router.
A mesh Wi-Fi system covers bigger homes far better than a range extender.
For a fixed desk, a network cable or powerline adapter beats any Wi-Fi.

remedies.title: Log in to my router's settings
remedies.why: The router has its own settings page or app for the Wi-Fi name, password and connected devices.

steps.text: Look at the sticker on the router for its address (often 192.168.1.1 or 192.168.0.1), login and app name.
Many routers now use an app (Eero, Google Home, Deco, your provider's app).
Find the router's address (the Default gateway / Router) in your network details.
Find the router's address in Network › Details › TCP/IP › Router.
If you change the Wi-Fi password, every device has to join again.

remedies.escalate: Office routers and firewalls belong to IT; don't change them.

remedies.title: Wired connection stuck at 100 Mbps
remedies.why: An old or damaged cable (only 4 of 8 wires working), an old switch, or a dock limits the link to 100 Mbps.

steps.text: Check the link speed: Network & internet › Ethernet › Link speed.
Check the link speed: Network › Ethernet › Details › Hardware.
Swap the cable for a Cat5e or Cat6 one; check the plug's clips and wires.
Try another port on the router/switch, or plug in without the dock.

remedies.title: Airplane mode is stuck on or greyed out
remedies.why: A hardware wireless switch, a stopped radio service, or a driver hiccup holds airplane mode on.

steps.text: Press the laptop's wireless key or switch (often Fn + a key with an aeroplane or antenna).
Turn airplane mode off in Settings.
Services › Radio Management Service › Restart.
Restart the computer (Restart, not Shut down).

remedies.title: Devices on the network stop working after the router restarts
remedies.why: The router hands out addresses that can change; printers, NAS drives and cameras set up by address then can't be found.

steps.text: In the router's settings, give the device a reserved address (DHCP reservation).
Or add the device by its name instead of its address, if it has one.
Remove and re-add the printer so it picks up the new address.

remedies.title: Mac Wi-Fi misbehaves on every network
symptoms: mac wifi not working any network
remedies.why: Damaged network settings on the Mac affect every network.

steps.text: Turn Wi-Fi off and on, then restart the Mac.
Network › Wi-Fi › ⋯ (bottom) › remove the Wi-Fi service, add it back with +, and join again.
Remove VPN, proxy and security tool network extensions you don't use (Login Items & Extensions › Network Extensions).
Run Wireless Diagnostics.
